How MV games are made; smooth and efficient
Each module with its written-out name and its abbreviation. For a quick look while playing, FPS and frame time are usually enough; the others help to find out why a game stutters or gets slow.
How many images the game draws per second. RPG Maker MV games are made for 60; with the 60 fps limit the value should stay at 60. Lower values look less smooth.

Time between two images on screen, in milliseconds: 16.7 ms equals 60 fps. The average shows the usual pace, max the longest gap. In the graph every frame is a point; dashed lines mark the target frame time (16.7 ms at 60 fps, 33.3 ms at 30 fps) and twice that; orange dots are frames that took longer than two target frames. Such spikes are felt as stutter even when the fps value looks fine.

The frame rate of the slowest 1 % of frames in the last update: it reveals stutter that an average hides. Slow counts frames that took longer than two target frames (33 ms at 60 fps, 67 ms at 30 fps).

Logic: game steps per second. MV runs its game logic at 60 steps per second, independent of the frame rate; fewer means the game itself runs slower. Hz: how often the screen asked for a new image; in brackets the refresh rate of the display.

How long the game\'s JavaScript needs per image (game logic and drawing commands). At 60 fps one frame has 16.7 ms; when this value gets close, the game cannot keep up. The graphics chip\'s work is not included.
Memory used by the game\'s JavaScript, and the limit the WebView allows. A value that keeps rising over a long session can point to a memory leak in the game; close to the limit the game may crash.
How many images the game keeps loaded (characters, tiles, pictures) and their size in megapixels. MV clears this cache itself; very high values cost memory.
Memory of the app itself (menus, overlay, on-screen controls). The game runs in Android\'s separate WebView process, so its memory shows under JS memory, not here.
Charge level, whether the phone is charging (+), and the battery temperature. Warm batteries (above about 40 °C) age faster, and phones often slow down when they are hot.

Android\'s own warning level for heat: none, light, moderate, severe, critical, emergency, shutdown. From moderate on, phones usually lower their speed, so the frame rate can drop. Heat: how close the phone is to severe throttling (100 %), as Android estimates it for the next seconds; not every phone reports it.
How the game is drawn (WebGL, WebGL 2 or Canvas, see Settings → Renderer) and the graphics chip the WebView uses. If WebGL 2 could not start, it says so.
Time of day, and how long you have been playing since this game was started (time in the app\'s menus counts, time with the app in the background does not).
Time the HUD itself needs per update to read and draw its values. It only runs when new values arrive and stays well below one millisecond.
The renderer decides how the game draws its pictures. WebGL is right for almost every game; the other two are alternatives for when something looks or runs wrong.
always try this first; it is how the game runs on PC too.
Fast, uses the graphics chip, and every effect works: lighting, fog, Mode 7 and filter plugins.
On a few devices the graphics driver has bugs, for example flickering or black pictures.
a game shows graphics errors, stays black or crashes with WebGL, or for very simple games without effects.
A simpler, very robust way of drawing that works the same almost everywhere.
Slower when many characters and effects are on screen; lighting, Mode 7 and filter plugins are missing or do not work.
WebGL causes problems on your device, or out of curiosity.
The newer version of WebGL; on some devices a little more stable or faster.
Experimental: the drawing library of RPG Maker MV games is made for WebGL 1, so usually you will not see a difference. If it cannot start, the app uses WebGL automatically.
A change applies the next time the game starts. The performance HUD (Renderer module) shows which one is running.
Saves battery; motion is less smooth

RPG Maker MV games always calculate their game logic 60 times per second. The frame rate only decides how many of those moments are drawn. The game runs at the same speed and the play time stays correct at every setting.
you play for a long time on battery or the phone gets warm.
Saves battery and keeps the phone cooler; the game itself is not slower.
Movement looks less smooth, most visible when walking or scrolling.
almost always; it is the default.
Exactly how MV games are made: every moment of the game logic is drawn once. Smooth without wasting power.
a game or plugin smooths motion between logic steps itself (rare), or for testing.
Draws as often as the screen refreshes, for example 120 times per second.
Experimental: with normal MV games the same picture is drawn twice without looking smoother, and the battery drains faster.
A change applies immediately, even during a game. The performance HUD shows the actual frame rate.
